moat_against: Consumer Products toys are commoditized against Mattel, LEGO and private label, with retailer bargaining power — the $1,021.9M 2025 goodwill impairment in that segment is the accounting receipt
Tariff exposure on imported toy product and retailer order caution
Magic growth is set-cycle driven (Universes Beyond cadence); management guided Magic lower in Q4 2026 on a tough comp and a set shifting to early 2027
Leverage plus a $0.70/qtr dividend commitment limit flexibility in a downturn
Entertainment segment is shrinking (−20% in Q2 2026) and digital games just took a $56M impairment on cancelled projects
moat_for: Magic: The Gathering — 30+ year franchise, record revenue in 2025 (+59%) and first $500M+ quarter in Q2 2026, with player network effects and a hobby-store distribution network rivals cannot replicate
Wizards segment economics: ~41–45% operating margins and high-30s/40% targeted through 2027 — proven pricing power
Dungeons & Dragons plus D&D Beyond digital platform — category-defining RPG IP with licensing reach
Owned IP library (Monopoly, Transformers, Play-Doh, Peppa Pig, My Little Pony) monetized asset-light through licensing, incl. MONOPOLY GO! royalties
moat_justification: A tale of two businesses: Wizards (Magic, D&D) is a genuine franchise moat — durable player network effects, pricing power, 40%+ segment margins — while Consumer Products toys are close to moatless and just absorbed a $1,021.9M goodwill impairment. Consolidated ROIC (fundamentals.json roic_proxy) is unstable rather than wide-moat-like: 26.4% in 2016, 5.0–9.4% in 2020–22, −30.3% in 2023 (eOne-era losses/impairments), 14.1% in 2024, 0.3% in 2025 (goodwill impairment in operating income) — the cash OE series is steadier than reported ROIC because the charges are non-cash, but a 7+ moat needs returns that stay above the cost of capital through a cycle, and Hasbro's printed history does not show that at the consolidated level. Gross margin has actually improved (62.0% in 2016 → 75.8% in 2025) on mix shift toward Wizards/licensing, which supports a moderate 5 rather than a weak score.
name: HASBRO, INC.
one_liner: Two-speed IP company (Magic/D&D strong, toys weak), moat 5/10 — even on the stepped-up TTM base it returns 11.4% weighted (IV@15% $69.29 vs $98.76 price), so it does not clear 15% until ~$69; on the normalized median base it is a D.
sector: Consumer Discretionary / Toys, games & IP licensing
